findings.description: [qodo] Startup banner always uses `git rev-parse HEAD` for the SHA, so reviews targeting a non-HEAD head (`--head <sha>`, `--head WORKING`, or `--head INDEX`) are labeled with the current HEAD hash instead of the target being reviewed. Prefer deriving the abbreviated SHA from the resolved head/ref or omit it when the target is not HEAD.

[expert] Catching SystemExit here converts any SystemExit raised from the surrounding try into EXIT_CLI_ERROR plus a traceback. If argparse parse_args() or any legitimate sys.exit() is inside this try, --help/--version and clean exits will be misreported as internal errors. Keep this catch scoped to the pipeline dispatch only.

[expert] The banner computes _banner_timeout via effective_invoke_timeout_s(backend, None), while _banner_timeout_note is fed env.get('FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S'). If the second argument is the env override (the helper's contract), the printed timeout can be the default/backend value while the note claims it came from FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S. Pass the same env value used by the note to keep the diagnostic truthful.

[expert] Startup-banner assembly is inlined in _run, mixing diagnostic fallbacks with pipeline flow. Extract an _emit_startup_banner helper so the subprocess/exception handling is testable and _run remains focused on the pipeline.

[adversarial] _banner_timeout_note recomputes backend-vs-env precedence from _run's `env` mapping, while `_banner_timeout` is computed separately by `effective_invoke_timeout_s(backend, None)` at line 3046 (which likely reads `os.environ` directly). If `_run` is called with an env mapping that differs from `os.environ` (tests or embedding), the banner note can claim FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S was used or ignored when the resolver actually did the opposite. This is diagnostics-only but can mislead timeout debugging.

[adversarial] _repo_display_name runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` with a 5s timeout, and `_run` later runs another `git rev-parse HEAD` with another 5s timeout. Both are serialized before the lock. On a machine where git is slow or hanging this adds up to 10 seconds of startup latency for a diagnostic banner that is supposed to be cheap and non-crashing.
